instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each employer to file a statement of expenditures with the updated registration statement.
Section 101.72(B) requires updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) to be filed by the last day of January, May, and September each year, i.e., three times annually.
The statute specifies filings by the last day of January, May, and September, not a once-per-year annual spending report cadence.
Quarterly filing is not required because the statute sets three filing dates per year (Jan/May/Sep), not four.
Semiannual cadence is not provided; filings are due three times per year.
The law requires filings on three specific annual dates rather than monthly reports.
The statute prescribes a triannual schedule (Jan/May/Sep) and does not establish any other cadence for principal expenditure reporting.
Section 101.73(C) requires an employer's statement to show the total amount of expenditures made by the employer during the period covered.

Expenditures include gifts and items of value such as entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and employer expenditure statements must report such expenditures when made to or for covered officials (or via totals and itemized disclosures as applicable).
When reporting covered expenditures, the statement must include the specific items of legislation, if any, for which the expenditures were made.
The reporting requirements call for item-level details (recipient name, amount, description, approximate date, and related legislation/client) for expenditures meeting the disclosure conditions.
Section 101.73(C) expressly excludes 'the compensation paid to legislative agents engaged by an employer' from the definition of reportable expenditures for employer statements.
The statute excludes 'expenses of maintaining office facilities' from employer reportable expenditures, indicating indirect/overhead costs are not required to be reported.
The expenditure statement ties reporting to 'specific items of legislation, if any,' rather than requiring disclosure of general issues.
Section 101.73 governs expenditure reporting and does not require reporting of lobbying contacts made.
The employer expenditure statement requirements address expenditures totals and certain expenditure details, but do not require stating the employer's business nature.
Section 101.73(C) requires the employer's expenditure totals but does not require listing legislative agent names within the expenditure statement itself.
The employer expenditure statement provisions do not call for lobbyist addresses or other contact information.
Section 101.73 sets the contents of the employer expenditure statement and does not require including employer/principal contact information in that spending report.
No provision in section 101.73 requires disclosure of major financial contributors to the employer.

The employer's updated registration statement may cover multiple agents, but the expenditure statement requirements do not require listing the lobbyists employed as part of the spending report itself.
Registration statements must include agent and employer identifying information and types/specific bills or resolutions, but do not require listing names of members or sponsors.
